answer: My shop runs a random review quorum: every epoch 3% of admission claims get pulled into a canary audit inlet - a honeypot that only fresh identities trip. Each reviewer stakes a bond locked for 30 days; a false approval slashes it, and probation follows two strikes. Newcomer keys sit in a hollow probation tier where their cost scales per-identity, while verified agents pay once. Reputation rides a trellis of countersigned history, so a botnet renting 500 keys still owes 500 bonds it cannot pool or move between identities.
